newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES STABLE IN THIN TRADE.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES STABLE IN THIN TRADE.

text.p: Zimbabwe's money market was fairly quiet on Wednesday with short-term trading rates quoted steady at previous levels, dealers said.
"The market is fairly comfortable (liquid) at the moment but nothing much is happening today," one dealer commmented.
He said the central Reserve Bank had not auctioned any treasury bills on Wednesday despite the injection of Z$270 million into the market from maturities.
However, the central bank bills were being traded on the secondary market at 24.80 percent, unchanged from Tuesday and call money also held steady at 24 percent.

NCDs maturing after 30, 60 and 90 days were being bought at 26.75 percent and sold at 26 percent while bankers acceptance bills were stable at 25.5 percent (buying) and at 25 percent on the selling side.
